I don't do anything to try and make up for it afterward like throwing up or fasting—I just sit there in the quiet feeling gross and ashamed of myself.\n\nDoctor: Do these eating episodes happen at least once a week for the past 3 months, or are they less frequent than that?\n\nPatient: Yes, they happen much more than once a week—it's pretty much every night, or at least several times a week. It's been going on for about three months now, starting around when my divorce was finalized and I transitioned to this new office role.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel very distressed or upset by these eating episodes, and have you noticed any significant weight changes since they started?\n\nPatient: I feel deeply ashamed and beat myself up every time it happens, and it's gotten to the point where I avoid going out with my buddies because I'm so embarrassed. I've never been one for strict dieting, fasting, or using things like laxatives and vomiting. It's just not something I've ever done.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had times when you deliberately tried to lose weight or control your shape by strict dieting, fasting, vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise?\n\nPatient: No, I've never tried any of those things to control my shape or weight.
